label: models/fw_console.mdl: a control console, waist high, dials, two screens, a row of switches

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/sentry.mdl, models/w_egon.mdl, models/filecabinet.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, D, A, C where the asset was D, B, B, D: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Reads as a waist-high control box: a square body with a flanged cap, two recessed screens and a switch row on the front, and four knobs on top. The outline has no fault in any view, and the brief's words give no slope to check it against.

M2.reason: Measured 45.3 x 31.5 x 40.2 against the asked 40 high (height 40.2, within 0.5%). Length and width are not asked for, so only the height is checked.

M3.reason: Brief-named parts all present: two screens (recessed dark panels, front-left and front), a row of six yellow switches on the front, and four chrome dials on the cap. Nothing a Valve console of this kind shows is missing. The dials sit on top rather than the front panel, which the brief does not fix.

M4.reason: Olive-grey painted steel body, grey metal cap, yellow switches and dark glass-like screens. This fits the brief's rusted steel and hazard yellow in Half-Life's palette.

M5.reason: The cap's radial streak texture (top and edges of the top view) reads as a smear rather than brushed or rusted steel. The body's large side faces are bare, with only a thin bevel line, so the wear the brief asks for is thin.

M6.reason: Line-up test: in four asks with the asset at D, B, B, D, the judges picked B, D, A, C. The asset was never picked as the one not made by Valve. Scored 2 by the rule that caps M6 here.

M7.reason: Upright, stands flat on its base (the below view is a closed flat plate). The switches and screens face the same way, so the front reads clearly. The brief names no front to check against.

M8.reason: 428 triangles against a bound of 476 (twice Half-Life's median of 238, more than the three-quarter mark of 291). Nothing open in the views a player sees: cap, body and underside are closed, and the knobs sit on the cap. The yellow switch tabs protruding at the side edges (left and right views) are attached.
